newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine court indicts CIADEA head-reports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine court indicts CIADEA head-reports.

text.p: An Argentine court late Thursday indicted the president of automaker CIADEA, Manual Antelo, for allegedly smuggling vehicles, local news agencies reported Friday.
The Cordoba Province Court of Appeals overturned a ruling last year that acquitted Antelo of the charges of "aggravated smuggling" to and from Uruguay, Chile and Peru, state-run agency Telam said.
CIADEA makes Renault cars under license.
The court banned Antelo from leaving the country, Telam said. Private news agency DyN added it also froze $1.5 million in assets.

Antelo and two other CIADEA officials were investigated for pressumably sending van autoparts abroad, collecting export enhancement reimbursements and then importing the vehicles back assembled into Argentina.
The prosecutor said the firm may have received up to $15 million in reimbursements, Telam said. DyN put them at up to $40 million.
The investigation was initiated by Cordoba's customs service..
Six other CIADEA officials were acquitted.
CIADEA officials were not immediately available for comment.
